title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
This page is Problem II of E443. A uniform elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) of length a is free at end A (x=0) and pinned at end B (x=a), meaning it is held by a pin about which it can turn freely. Euler seeks its normal modes.

The separated solution is y = cos(θ²t)·[A cos(θx/b) + B sin(θx/b) + C e^{θx/b} + D e^{−θx/b}].

Free end (x=0). Zero shear and zero moment (y''=y'''=0) give A = C+D and B = C−D; this was done on the previous page.

Pinned end (x=a), with ζ = θa/b:
(i) Force balance gives the pin reaction G = Kc²(θ³/b³) cos(θ²t)(A sin ζ − B cos ζ + C e^ζ − D e^{−ζ}). This is just the end shear, i.e. the force the pin must exert.
(ii) Zero bending moment (y''=0): A cos ζ + B sin ζ − C e^ζ − D e^{−ζ} = 0.
(iii) Zero deflection: A cos ζ + B sin ζ + C e^ζ + D e^{−ζ} = 0.

Adding and subtracting (ii) and (iii) gives A cos ζ + B sin ζ = 0 and C e^ζ + D e^{−ζ} = 0. Euler normalizes with C = e^{−ζ}, D = −e^{ζ}. He notes these must be multiplied by an infinitesimal line segment so that y stays small: this is the linearization / small-amplitude normalization. Then A = e^{−ζ} − e^{ζ} and B = e^{−ζ} + e^{ζ}.

Substituting gives the frequency equation e^{−ζ}(cos ζ + sin ζ) = e^{ζ}(cos ζ − sin ζ). Equivalent forms:
- tan ζ = tanh ζ;
- e^{2ζ} = (cos ζ + sin ζ)/(cos ζ − sin ζ) = tan(½ρ + ζ). Here Euler's ρ denotes a right angle (π/2), so this is tan(π/4 + ζ).

On the next page Euler gets the roots ζ ≈ 5ρ/2 − ω, 9ρ/2, 13ρ/2, … with ω ≈ e^{−5ρ} ≈ 0.000388, i.e. ζ₁ = 3.92666 and so on. These are the standard free–pinned (equivalently clamped–pinned) beam eigenvalues.
errors: No substantive errors. The first displayed balance equation omits the time factor cos(θ²t) that appears in the expression for G; this is harmless. The derivation and the identity (cos ζ + sin ζ)/(cos ζ − sin ζ) = tan(π/4 + ζ), with ρ = π/2, are correct.

ideas.what: Boundary conditions for a pinned (hinged) end: zero deflection and zero bending moment, with the pin reaction equal to the shear force
ideas.modern_name: Simply-supported / hinged boundary conditions for the Euler–Bernoulli beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (beam vibration papers 1744–1774), with Daniel Bernoulli
ideas.where_published: E443 itself (Novi Comm. 17); also earlier Euler work on elastic laminae; discussed by Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11/2)

ideas.what: Frequency equation tan ζ = tanh ζ for the free–pinned beam, with asymptotic roots (4k+1)π/4 and an exponentially small correction
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic equation of free–hinged (and clamped–hinged) beam: tan βL = tanh βL

ideas.what: Normalizing the eigenvector and multiplying by an infinitesimal 'lineola' to keep the motion linear and small
ideas.where_published: E443 and Euler's other vibration papers

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard derivation of the free–pinned beam frequency equation tan ζ = tanh ζ. It is well known and credited to Euler's E443 in Truesdell's history; nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. Note for readers: 'ρ' in 'Tang.(½ρ + ζ)' is Euler's notation for a right angle (π/2), so ½ρ = π/4; the transcription correctly keeps ½.
